analysis.title: GS Basics - Nvidia. Positioning. Fed Hawkishness
key_insights: Weekend Asian support measures (China lower margin requirements, Korea eased buyback limits, Taiwan tighter short selling rules) helped markets bounce, but such measures are not what you want to see marking a bottom.

Trump administration comments on Nvidia are more meaningful. Bessent distinguished selling compute to China from supplying the Chinese military and left the door open to Jensen's return, conditional on the compliance investigation.

Author cautions against confusing a rhetorical pivot with regulatory relief. Remote access restrictions are still defended, investigations remain active, and the real test is licenses for offshore data centers.
Last week's selloff was driven by Nvidia export restrictions, remote compute access, TSMC licensing uncertainty and an AI backdrop weakened by growth deceleration and accounting questions.
Prime brokerage data show nets cut sharply, gross up and substantial shorts added into the decline, with the largest shorting since April 2025. Breaking the 200d triggered further de-risking.
Investors now hold meaningful shorts, which the author calls the missing ingredient, so a bear market rally setup is obvious. The open question is whether to sell into it or let it run.

VIX nearly hit 40 into the weekend with CNN Fear & Greed near 10, put/call near the 95th percentile, CFTC leveraged funds reportedly net short Nasdaq futures and the steepest VIX curve inversion since April 2025. Vol normalization is itself a tailwind.
Historically VIX closes above 35 often preceded positive equity reversals over following weeks, though the author flags small samples and not a forecast.

Author argues the Fed is mispriced. Market prices a growth shock and AI capex slowdown, commodities have collapsed, inflation expectations are near yearly lows, real rates look too high and financial conditions have tightened materially.
Hope rests on Kevin Warsh, and the first FOMC member to acknowledge the tightening is expected to provoke an outsized reaction. Bessent has already raised the risk of a Fed policy mistake.
Parallels with Nov/Dec 2018 are increasingly clear. Financial conditions have tightened faster this cycle, though the 2018 equity drawdown was deeper before bottoming.
Credit is the tell. If Nvidia rallies but neocloud spreads stay under pressure, the move is likely short covering. AI infrastructure is increasingly dependent on external capital as its cost rises.

Calendar: Flash PMIs Monday, Dell Tuesday, Beige Book and core PCE Wednesday, then payrolls, the December FOMC and November CPI. Thanksgiving shortens the US week and thin liquidity may amplify a squeeze.
Net view: extreme positioning, elevated vol, a potential Nvidia policy pivot and a more visible Trump put create a compelling tactical setup.

tension_points.bull_case: Extreme positioning, VIX near 40, heavy new shorts and Trump put support a tactical rally, and VIX closes above 35 have often preceded positive reversals.
tension_points.bear_case: Rhetorical pivot is not regulatory relief, AI financing depends on costlier external capital, and a rally may only be short covering.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Neocloud spreads staying under pressure while Nvidia rallies, or no licenses granted for offshore data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Tight financial conditions, collapsed commodities and low inflation expectations mean hawkish rhetoric will look backward looking if November CPI is near expectations.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed rhetoric is clearly hawkish and the Fed may not acknowledge tightening quickly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot November CPI or core PCE print would undercut the dovish pivot case.
